correctness.rationale: For m,r>=2,n>=3r and inclusive shortest-path graph-metric VR(K_m square C_n;r), the product distance is d_Cn(i,j)+1_{a!=b}. Core B consists of faces with column diameter <=r−1; full clique fibers collapse by dominated-vertex pairs to VR(C_n;r−1)≈S1, with fixed-color rim degree one since (r−1)/n<1/3. Every distance-r pair must lie in one color. Its common neighboring columns are the clockwise intermediate r−1 columns, except for a third same-color column at i+2r when n=3r. Accordingly every noncore face lies in one full simplex F_{i,a} on the long edge and the intervening column vertices, or is one of exactly mr exceptional isolated maximal triangles. F_{i,a}∩B is the endpoint-edge boundary joined with a nonempty simplex and distinct F meet only in B. Pair noncore faces with their pivot-extended faces, descending in dimension, giving U↘B. Each exceptional triangle boundary winds one time around the rim because each long edge is homotopic relative endpoints through its F simplex to r consecutive same-row edges. Attaching mr degree-one 2-cells to S1 kills its fundamental group and leaves wedge^{mr−1}S2; if n>3r there are no such triangles. Verified exact m=2,r=2 boundary and stable cases; no assertion about r=1 or n<3r. This argument is uniform and not dependent on finite sampling.

value.rationale: A sharp and motivated all-integer-scale resonance for the natural graph-metric product K_m square C_n, including thin toroidal grids at m=3 and circular ladders at m=2. No unsupported full-filtration claim is made.
